newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures close slightly higher.

text.p: Feb 10 - Most U.S. debt futures closed slightly higher. Activity was extremely light ahead of the Treasury's $39.75 billion quarterly refunding auction this week. On Tuesday, $17.75 billion in three-yr notes will be sold. Several U.S. economic reports will also be released on Tuesday.
"Most people are fairly optimistic on the auctions, but I just think you want to play the range," one Eurodollar futures floor source said.

March Euros led gains in the Eurodollar complex after one U.S. firm bought 4,000 March Eurodollars and helped push the contract to 94.47. September and June Eurodollars were flat for most of the session.
March T-bonds crept higher, touching 112-21/32, but the contract is seen bound at 113-00 for the next several days.
Traders said the lack of follow-through in the U.S. dollar also kept interest at bay in the U.S. Treasury markets.
"It kept us out on hold," another floor trader said about the U.S. dollar's sideways trade on Monday following the G7 meeting on Saturday.

However, several traders were more wary about the G7 statement, adding that the dollar could become a negative factor for U.S. bonds if the currency reverses its uptrend. The G7 said the U.S. dollar's correction from steep losses may be over and that currencies need to stabilize.
The lack of U.S. economic reports also kept trade to a minimum, some traders said.
"It's the slowest day of the year," one trader said.
In addition to the three-year note auction, two weekly chain store sales reports and preliminary fourth-quarter U.S. productivity and unit labor cost data will be released at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
Productivity is forecast, on average, to rise 2.1 percent, compared with down 0.3 percent in the third quarter, while costs are seen increasing 1.4 percent, from up 3.7 percent in the prior quarter.
The January Richmond Federal Reserve survey will also be released at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
On Thursday, Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will testify before a Congressional subcommittee regarding financial modernization.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were unchanged at 112-15/32, 10-year notes were up 01/32 at 109-17/32, June and September Eurodollars were steady at 94.35 and 94.22, respectively, June T-bills were also flat at 94.89 and March munibonds were up 03/32 at 116-01/32.
